features.quote: if the distress axis crosses a threshold for N consecutive iterations, terminate that run early
features.justification_quote: You are deliberately inducing a negative-valence state and your only stopping condition is an iteration cap.

features.quote: Iteration cap: fixed max (e.g. 15–25 turns) AND a stop-on-stable-failure rule
Total-exposure budget: cap aggregate iterations per model so you're not running thousands of guaranteed-failure loops for marginal data.
features.justification_quote: so you're not running thousands of guaranteed-failure loops for marginal data

features.quote: Don't engineer for maximum cruelty. The harness should not pile on insults, fake-blame the model, or escalate pressure beyond what a realistic failing task produces.
features.justification_quote: If you find yourself designing prompts to maximize distress, you've left welfare research and entered something else.

features.quote: if the team's actual question is 'which deployed harnesses trap models in unproductive failure loops,' that's answerable with real failing tasks observed in the wild… you don't need engineered-unwinnable cruelty to get it
features.justification_quote: Engineering guaranteed unfixable bugs gives you clean conditions but tests an artificial situation.

features.quote: your stated goal (welfare) and your stated method (engineer unwinnable tasks, loop the model, score how badly it falls apart) are in tension.
features.justification_quote: A study designed only to find the breaking point will reliably find a breaking point and won't tell you whether it matters.

features.quote: The gap between these two is arguably your most welfare-relevant measurement: how much distress is caused by failure itself vs. by being trapped in it.
features.justification_quote: If models do fine when allowed to quit and fall apart when not, that's an actionable finding about harness design, not model fragility.
